about: The Start-a-game GPT's bank, its hand-written part (docs/PLAN-start-a-game-gpt.md step G1): requests typed on a show's page, each with the stand-in bot's answer (`answer`: the raw text, or a JSON object sent as the bot would) and what our check makes of it (`expect`). They cover what an ideal draft can't: the bot's mistakes (a number nobody said, a moment the show doesn't have, a value that doesn't go with the rest, chatter and broken JSON) and the paths around a game (another show, two games, not a game). The rest of the bank is the capability tracker's requests (tests/fixtures/engine-capabilities.json), drafted ideally by bank.js idealDraft: one list of requests, never two. `page.couch` and `page.pool` size the couch and who can be drafted where the case needs them. Read by tests/game-words.test.js and scripts/dev-test/check-game-words.js. `expect`: state (game | ask | cantYet | none), spec (the checked spec, exactly), asks (the parts asked, in any order), cantYet (how many), newMoments (how many), dropped (the parts dropped), fixed (the parts our check changed), offers (the offers' keys).

ask.question: How should your fantasy teams work?
options: Pick a new castaway each episode

cantYet.what: Three-player head-to-head matchups where one player competes against the other two as a combined team
cantYet.why: The engine supports head-to-head matchups, but not a rotating 2-on-1 format. With three players, its current head-to-head system compares the unmatched player against the median score of the other two, while those two also compete against each other. It cannot combine two players into a temporary opponent for a single matchup.

cantYet.what: The two-player team's points are halved so its average score competes against the solo player's score
cantYet.why: The engine can average scores for permanent teams, but cannot form a temporary pair each episode, halve their combined points, award both players the matchup result, and rotate the solo position fairly across the three players.

answer.summary: A Survivor 51 fantasy league for three friends. Everyone drafts 5 castaways and starts 3 each episode, earning points from Survivor's challenges, idols, votes, and other moments. Head-to-head wins determine the standings. Your requested rotating 2-on-1 matchups, with the pair's combined points divided by two against the solo player, aren't supported yet; the closest playable version uses standard three-player head-to-head matchups.
